# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - The ebb and flow of market sentiment over the exact state of health of the European political scene dominated movements in metal prices in the first half of November. In more normal times, the fall of two European Governments might be seen as either clearly bullish or clearly bearish. On this occasion, however, a jittery market could not really decide which should be the case. Gold seemed to benefit from this shaky sentiment, adding $100 in a few days at one point, and, despite the usual worries about a slow global economy, the other metals all obediently followed gold higher. • The sense that the precious metal complex may have been oversold was reinforced by a bounce in speculative futures holdings in all four major precious metals in the first week of November. While gold appears to be the motor driving investor interest across the sector, positioning remains relatively low by 2011 standards for the other three metals suggesting that investors could yet return to the markets in greater numbers, driving prices higher. - In the ETF sector, gold saw continued buying as risk aversion was heightened over the excruciatingly slow progress being made in addressing European sovereign debt issues. The other three metals saw small decreases in outstanding ETF holdings. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** ##### **15 November 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **15 November 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 08 November 2011; ETF data to 11 November 2011.** **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Early in the month, the eccentric decision by the Greek Prime Minister to call for a referendum on the Greek bailout sent gold surging higher as EURUSD failed to respond. On the 3rd, the European Central Bank cut interest rates. Although this would normally weaken the currency, the perception that at least something positive was being done for the European economy sent the Euro higher, impelling gold to $1,760 that day. Gold continued to a brief high of $1,800 on the 8th. However, on the 9th it fell backwards: Italy’s attempt to pass an emergency budget failed to convince the markets and Italian bond yields soared and the Euro slumped. Gold crashed to $1,745 on the 10th before Prime Minister Berlusconi revealed plans to step down. The market relaxed a little at the prospect of a more technocratic Italian Government and the Euro recovered its poise, allowing gold’s safe haven credentials to reassert themselves once again. • In the gold market, investor interest rose for the third successive week with net long speculative positions on COMEX climbing by 2.4 million ounces to 24.6 million ounces. Open interest increased at the same time, demonstrating the opening of fresh long positions and suggesting that gold could yet make another push towards the $1,900 level this year. • Gold ETF holdings climbed for the fifth week in a row, their longest positive run since July. We interpret bouts of gold buying through these vehicles as signals of market stress and risk aversion which are related, in this case, to the escalation of the European debt crisis. Currently there _seems_ relatively little prospect of any resolution to this problem being developed and we could see further ETF buying in the coming weeks to lift holdings from their current 69.1 million ounces to record levels. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—November 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Silver essentially followed the tracks of the gold price in the first two weeks of November with little regard for its own fundamentals. As gold gained $100, silver added over $2 on risk aversion while European leaders argued over the Greek proposal for a referendum on the bailout. Diplomatic language was pushed to its limits before the Greek Government transformed into a coalition of national unity. Silver peaked at $35.30 on the 8th as gold reached $1,800 but fell back as attention switched to Italy, weakening the Euro. Silver dropped back to $33.50 on the 10th before the prospect of a new Italian Government assuaged investors’ fears, allowing silver to gain some stability. This news-driven roller-coaster pattern of price movements seems set to continue in coming weeks. Interestingly, the gold:silver ratio is slowly moving in gold’s favour at the moment so underperformance by the grey metal may be the cur

rent trend. - Net long speculative interest in silver on COMEX increased by 11.1 million ounces to 159 million ounces in the week to the 8th of November. With price action having been choppy, no clear trend has been established in silver positions over recent weeks. However, open interest is gradually increasing, suggesting that investor interest is slowly retuning as market volatility becomes somewhat more manageable. - Silver ETF positioning fell by 8 million ounces last week to 462 million ounces. The only fund which showed significant changes in holdings was in the iShares fund which suggests that this may have been a single entity selling metal with sentiment remaining more positive elsewhere in the market. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **15 November 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 08 November 2011; ETF data to 11 November 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- The platinum price followed that of gold in the first two weeks of November. The spread between the two metals widened in gold’s favour, moving from $120 per ounce to $140 as risk aversion became a more important feature of the market. Nonetheless, as gold climbed, platinum climbed, regardless of positive or negative newsflow related to its own fundamentals. Having dipped as low as $1,560 on the 1st of November following the short-lived call for a Greek referendum, platinum brief

ly bounced through the $1,600 level the following day. The next move came on the 3rd when market sentiment welcomed the ECB’s decision to cut rates. This firmed the Euro and improved the prospects for European manufacturing demand for the platinum group metals, sending platinum surging to $1,640 later that day. In the following days, though, gold became more important once again as Greek concerns persisted. Gold rose to $1,800 and platinum moved more gingerly towards $1,670 on the 8th. A weaker Euro send platinum plunging down to $1,609 on the 10th, testing investors’ nerves but it has since recovered some ground. - Japanese investors cut their TOCOM positions strongly in late October and early November, trimming them from 250,000 ounces to 170,000 ounces. On NYMEX, sentiment was much more positive with 114,000 ounces of net long positions added in the same two week period, taking the total to 1.23 million ounces. Despite concerns over the global economic outlook, the rising gold price seems to have added some conviction to many investors’ bullish longer term views on platinum. - Platinum ETF holdings slipped 600 ounces lower to 1.48 million ounces during the week to the 11th of November. In contrast to palladium, some buying was seen in North America but this was offset by selling in the London ETFS fund, leaving the week almost neutral in terms of net metal movements. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **15 November 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 08 November 2011; ETF data to 11 November 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

Despite ETF selling and negative news stories over the disruptions caused to the Japanese carmakers’ output from the Thai floods, the sense that palladium had been oversold to unsustainably low levels began to develop. Buyers below these levels could prove to have chosen wisely although further volatility can be expected. Palladium traded in a $625 to $675 range with the low being recorded on the 1st after the short-lived Greek refer

endum proposal was made. On fundamental grounds, there seemed little reason for palladium to gain ground after this but a rising gold price dragged all the other metals higher. Palladium spiked $30 from $640 to $670 on the 3rd when the ECB revealed an unexpected rate cut. The general trend, though, was for higher precious metal prices and palladium peaked just above $675 on the 8th as the prices of its sister metals reached their high points too. Italian woes became the market’s focus the following day and palladium dropped back to $640 on the 10th, following the Euro. Positive price action since then sees it trading at $659 now. - Net long positions in palladium continued to rise from their very low end-September level in the first week of November. They climbed by a further 67,000 ounces following the previous week’s increase of 17,000 ounces. While positions remain very low by 2011 standards, there must be some scope for further investor-driven price appreciation in the remaining weeks of the month. - Palladium ETF holdings fell by 11,700 ounces in the week to the 11th of November, dropping to 1.88 million ounces. Once again, small amounts of European buying were outweighed by North American selling. Since one year ago, the two largest European funds have shed 85,000 ounces (although this has been offset by the addition of 70,000 ounces into the Julius Baer fund).
